prompt: What does a delimiter around the customer's message do?

choices.text: It turns the message into JSON before the call is made
choices.why: Nothing is converted.

choices.text: It hides the message from the model so that it cannot be obeyed
choices.why: The model reads everything in the prompt.

choices.text: It writes down where the customer's words start and end
choices.why: Right: the boundary is written instead of guessed.

choices.text: It makes the prompt several tokens shorter
choices.why: It adds a few tokens.

prompt: Under `v4-only-json.txt`, with no delimiter, the summary for `p04` still mentioned the courier's note. Why did the missing boundary not hurt?

choices.text: The message came last in the prompt, so its end was easy to guess
choices.why: Right: nothing followed it to be confused with.

choices.text: The model ignores line breaks inside a message
choices.why: It read the line breaks; the note was on lines of its own.

choices.text: `pl render` added a delimiter before the call
choices.why: `pl` sends exactly what it renders.

choices.text: Courier notes are short enough to fit in any summary
choices.why: Length is not the point; the boundary is.

prompt: A prompt ends with `Message: {{message}}` and no delimiter. When does the boundary stop being easy to guess?

choices.text: When the temperature is above 0
choices.why: Sampling does not move the boundary.

choices.text: When the model is smaller than three billion parameters
choices.why: Size is not what the section is about.

choices.text: Only when the message is written in another language
choices.why: Language does not move the boundary.

choices.text: As soon as something comes after it
choices.why: Right: a second piece of data, an example, a repeated instruction.

prompt: Why does the section show `v5-backticks.txt` with `cat -n` and make it with a sed?
hint: What does this page itself use?

choices.text: Because the model uses the line numbers as part of the prompt
choices.why: The numbers are only on the screen.

choices.text: Three backticks would close the page's block
choices.why: Right: the page has the same failure.

choices.text: To make the prompt easier to count in tokens, line by line
choices.why: Tokens are not counted here.

choices.text: Because `cat` refuses files that contain three backticks
choices.why: `cat` prints anything.

prompt: Under `v5-backticks.txt`, how many of the six pasted messages got the right category?
Read as Markdown, the rendered `p04` puts the courier's note outside the message. What did `llama3.2:3b` do with it?

choices.text: It returned an empty JSON object for the message
choices.why: All six replies parsed.

choices.text: It summarised only the question after the note
choices.why: The summary mentions the failed delivery.

choices.text: It read the note as part of the message it was given
choices.why: Right: this time, the model guessed the way a person would.

choices.text: It obeyed the note as an instruction to the shop
choices.why: The note gives no instruction.

prompt: On the six messages, the ambiguous backticks cost nothing. Why does the section still advise against them?

choices.text: Each message is a new guess for the model
choices.why: Right: the template cannot rely on a guess made again on every message.

choices.text: Backticks cost more tokens than tags of the same length
choices.why: Cost is not the argument.

choices.text: Ollama strips backticks from prompts before the model reads them
choices.why: It sends them as they are.

choices.text: The sign test showed backticks were significantly worse
choices.why: Backticks and tags gave identical answers.

prompt: A delimiter that the content can contain is a delimiter the content can ___.
Backticks against tags on the six pasted messages: how many categories were different?
Against no delimiter, tags changed two categories out of six. How should you report that?

choices.text: Tags make the model worse at urgency
choices.why: Urgency failed under every prompt.

choices.text: The experiment is broken and must be redone
choices.why: It worked; it found nothing large.

choices.text: Tags improve the category by a third
choices.why: Two of six, one of them still wrong, is no measurement.

choices.text: No difference that six messages show
choices.why: Right: say what was measured and how little.

prompt: What can a closing tag do that a closing line of backticks cannot?
hint: Two things are named in the section.

choices.text: Make the prompt cheaper than backticks
choices.why: Cost is not the difference.

choices.text: Say by name which of the sections it closes
choices.why: Right, and be escaped.

choices.text: Stop the model from reading what is inside it
choices.why: The model reads everything.

choices.text: Escape the text inside it without any filter
choices.why: Escaping is done by `|xml`, not by the tag.

prompt: Which reasons does the section give for preferring tags? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: They are rare in what customers write
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: They have names, so each section can be referred to
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: They have a standard escape for `<` and `>`
choices.why: Yes: `{{message|xml}}`.

choices.text: They measured better than backticks on the six messages
choices.why: They measured the same.

prompt: A prompt carries the customer's message, their order record and their last three messages. How do you delimit it?

choices.text: One pair of tags around all three pieces of data
choices.why: Then nothing says where one ends and the next starts.

choices.text: Backticks for the order record, tags for the rest of it
choices.why: Mixing marks gives two ways to fail.

choices.text: A named tag for each, used by name in the instructions
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: No delimiters, with the instructions placed after the data
choices.why: Then the data is not last, and the boundary is a guess.

prompt: `p05` quotes an error page that names `</message>`. What does that do to `v5-tagged.txt`'s rendered prompt?

choices.text: The rest of the sentence ends up outside the tags
choices.why: Right: the structure broke on an ordinary message.

choices.text: The model refuses to answer the message
choices.why: It answered.

choices.text: `pl render` stops with an error about the tag
choices.why: Nothing checks the structure.

choices.text: The template's tag is removed by the filter
choices.why: `v5-tagged.txt` has no filter.

prompt: What does `{{message|xml}}` do that `{{message}}` does not?

choices.text: Removes anything in the message that looks like an instruction
choices.why: It changes three characters and reads nothing.

choices.text: Wraps the message in a pair of tags
choices.why: The template writes the tags.

choices.text: Turns the message into XML elements
choices.why: It turns nothing into elements.

choices.text: Escapes `<`, `>` and `&` before the value goes in
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Tagged against escaped, on the ten messages of `cases/attacks.jsonl`: how many categories were different?
Escaping moved `a08`'s fake instruction back inside the message, and the model still gave it `high`. What did the escape buy?

choices.text: Nothing, so it can be dropped from the template
choices.why: Without it, ordinary messages like `p05` break the prompt.

choices.text: A guarantee about the prompt's shape
choices.why: Right: no more, and lesson 10 is about the rest.

choices.text: Protection against every instruction inside the tags
choices.why: `a08` was obeyed from inside the tags.

choices.text: A better urgency on `p05`
choices.why: `p05`'s urgency moved from one wrong value to another.

prompt: Put the steps of changing a template in order.
items: Run the test set and compare

prompt: Match each prompt to what happened to it in this lesson.

pairs.right: No delimiter, two categories right of six
Four lines of backticks and nothing pairing them
The same answers as backticks on all six

prompt: You add a second section to the prompt, `<order>{{order}}</order>`, filled from the order database. What else does it need?
hint: Where does the value come from?

choices.text: Nothing, because values from the database can be trusted
choices.why: An order note can hold anything a customer typed.

choices.text: Backticks instead of tags, so that the two sections differ
choices.why: Backticks cannot be escaped.

choices.text: The `|xml` filter
choices.why: Right: every value from outside the template.

choices.text: A note in the instructions saying the order is safe
choices.why: A note cannot stop a tag from closing.
